mainTopic: A lender as שומר שכר, collateral and שמיטה, and the new משנה on those who swear and collect
overview: This amud finishes the chapter שבועת הדיינין and opens a new one. רב יוסף says a lender holding a משכון is like a שומר שכר, because he is busy with a מצוה and saves money on other מצוות. The גמרא asks whether רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא argue about his idea. It answers that everyone accepts it, and they argue only about a lender who uses the collateral for himself. Next the גמרא checks whether שמואל's rule, that collateral counts for the whole debt, is the subject of a dispute in a ברייתא about שמיטה. It rejects this: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and רבי יהודה הנשיא argue only about the collateral's own value, and collateral can serve simply as a reminder. Then a new משנה teaches that Torah oaths free the swearer from paying, but five people swear and collect. It explains the hired worker, the robbed person and the injured person, and רבי יהודה requires a partial admission in each case. The amud ends just as the משנה begins the case of an opponent who is suspected of swearing falsely, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רב יוסף: The lender is like a paid guard
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף rules that a lender holding a משכון has the status of a שומר שכר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יוסף says: the lender holding collateral is like a paid guard.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives his view on a lender who holds collateral. He says the lender counts as a paid guard, not an unpaid one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The view just before this held that the lender is only a שומר חנם (unpaid guard). רב יוסף disagrees. Taking care of the collateral is part of the מצוה of lending, and while he does it he is free from other מצוות that cost money. That saving counts as his 'pay', so he is a שומר שכר and is responsible if the collateral is lost.

keyTerms.meaning: A paid guard. He is responsible for theft and loss.
An unpaid guard. He is only responsible if he was careless.
Collateral: an item a borrower gives the lender to secure a loan
Is like, is compared to

steps.whyThisMatters: רב יוסף's reasoning relies on the well-known rule that one who is busy with a מצוה is exempt from other מצוות (עוסק במצוה פטור מן המצוה). His new point is that the money saved through this exemption can count as payment.

phrases.english: And Rav Yosef says:
He is like a paid guard.
phrases.notes: 'He' is the lender who is holding the borrower's collateral.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second opinion in a pair. It answers the view just before this text, which called the lender a שומר חנם.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A lender holding collateral has the status of a שומר שכר.

steps.title: Do the תנאים argue about רב יוסף's idea?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא may be arguing about רב יוסף's principle itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that רב יוסף's view is a dispute between תנאים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether the argument in the משנה is really about רב יוסף's idea. The next step will answer this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי עקיבא (the lender loses money) agrees with רב יוסף, then רבי אליעזר (the lender collects in full) would seem to reject רב יוסף. That would mean רב יוסף's view is disputed by a תנא. The גמרא does not like to make an אמורא's view depend on one side of a disagreement, so it checks this.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (a suggestion the גמרא is testing)
תנאים, the Sages of the משנה. 'תנאי היא' means 'it is a dispute between תנאים.'

phrases.english: Shall we say that Rav Yosef's view is a dispute of Tannaim?
phrases.notes: The תנאים here are רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא from the משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests whether רב יוסף's ruling is the same thing the משנה argues about.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the dispute between רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא depend on whether רב יוסף is right?

steps.title: No, everyone agrees with רב יוסף. They argue about a lender who uses the collateral
steps.stepSummary: Everyone accepts רב יוסף's idea for a guard of a lost item. The argument is about a lender who uses the collateral for himself: is he still doing a מצוה?
steps.simpleTranslation: No. For someone guarding a lost item, everyone holds like רב יוסף. Here they argue about a lender who needs the collateral and uses it. One Sage holds he is still doing a מצוה. The other Sage holds he is not doing a מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. Everyone accepts רב יוסף's principle. The argument is about a different, narrower case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is a lender who uses the collateral with the borrower's permission. רבי עקיבא says he is still doing a מצוה, so he is a שומר שכר. רבי אליעזר says that once he benefits from the item, he is guarding it for himself and not for the מצוה, so he is only a שומר חנם. So the argument is about the facts of this case, not about רב יוסף's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone guarding a lost item until the owner comes
Everyone agrees
Needs the collateral, meaning he uses it for himself
They disagree

steps.whatToRemember: Everyone agrees with רב יוסף's principle. רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא only argue about whether a lender who uses the collateral is still doing a מצוה.

phrases.english: No; regarding one who guards a lost item,

phrases.aramaic: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אִית לְהוּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף;
phrases.english: everyone holds like Rav Yosef;

phrases.aramaic: וְהָכָא בְּמַלְוֶה צָרִיךְ לְמַשְׁכּוֹן קָא מִיפַּלְגִי:
phrases.english: and here they disagree about a lender who needs the collateral:
phrases.notes: He uses the item with the borrower's permission, and pays for the use by taking it off the debt.

phrases.english: one Sage holds he is doing a מצוה,
phrases.notes: This is רבי עקיבא. Since he is doing a מצוה, he counts as a paid guard.

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר לָאו מִצְוָה קָא עָבֵיד.
phrases.english: and one Sage holds he is not doing a מצוה.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא; בְּשׁוֹמֵר אֲבֵידָה דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אִית לְהוּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion in step 2 by moving the argument to a narrower case.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that the תנאים argue about רב יוסף's principle itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The suggestion assumed the case was a plain lender. The argument is really about a lender who uses the collateral.

steps.title: A ברייתא about שמיטה and loans with collateral
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that שמואל's ruling about collateral is a dispute between תנאים. It quotes a ברייתא where רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and רבי יהודה הנשיא argue about whether שמיטה cancels a loan backed by collateral.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this is a dispute between תנאים? Someone lends to his friend with collateral, and the שמיטה year arrives. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: even if the collateral is worth only half the loan, שמיטה does not cancel the debt. רבי יהודה הנשיא says: if the collateral is worth as much as the debt, שמיטה does not cancel it. If not, שמיטה cancels it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to שמואל's ruling, which said the debt is cancelled if the lender loses the collateral. It quotes a ברייתא to see whether the תנאים already argue about this idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A loan backed by collateral is not cancelled by שמיטה. Here the collateral is worth less than the loan. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says the debt is still not cancelled. רבי יהודה הנשיא says it is not cancelled only if the collateral covers the whole debt. The גמרא will now look closely at what these words mean.

keyTerms.meaning: Like a dispute between תנאים
The seventh year, which cancels loans
Cancels the debt (through שמיטה)
Half
Equal in value to his debt

phrases.english: Shall we say it is like a dispute of Tannaim:
phrases.notes: The 'it' is שמואל's ruling that the debt is cancelled if the lender loses the collateral.

phrases.english: One who lends to his fellow on collateral
and the Shemitah year began,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ שָׁוֶה אֶלָּא פְּלַג –
phrases.english: even if it is worth only half,
phrases.notes: The collateral is worth only half of the loan.

phrases.english: it does not cancel.
These are the words of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel.
Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi says:
If his collateral was equal to his debt,
it does not cancel,
and if not, it cancels.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רב יוסף discussion and goes back to שמואל's ruling about lost collateral.
steps.raayaObject: Whether שמואל's view about collateral is a dispute between תנאים
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and רבי יהודה הנשיא on שמיטה and collateral

steps.title: What does the תנא קמא mean by 'does not cancel'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what exactly רבן שמעון בן גמליאל means when he says שמיטה does not cancel the debt.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the meaning of 'does not cancel' that the תנא קמא said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the exact meaning of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's words. This sets up the next step, where it will try out a reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Does not cancel' could mean two things. It could mean only the part of the debt that the collateral covers stays alive. Or it could mean the whole debt stays alive. The answer decides what the two תנאים are really arguing about.

keyTerms.meaning: The first תנא, the first opinion quoted (here רבן שמעון בן גמליאל)
What?

phrases.english: What does "does not cancel" mean
that the first Tanna says?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אֵינוֹ מְשַׁמֵּט דְּקָאָמַר תַּנָּא קַמָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks closely at the wording of the ברייתא just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does 'does not cancel' mean only the part equal to the collateral, or the whole debt?

steps.title: The first reading leads to a strange result
steps.stepSummary: Suppose רבן שמעון בן גמליאל means only the part equal to the collateral survives. Then רבי יהודה הנשיא would hold that even that part is cancelled. But then why take collateral at all?
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say he means the part equal to the collateral is not cancelled, then it follows that רבי יהודה הנשיא holds even the part equal to the collateral is cancelled! But then why would the lender take collateral?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the first reading of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and shows it cannot work. It would force a strange view on רבי יהודה הנשיא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבן שמעון בן גמליאל only protects the part of the debt the collateral covers, then רבי יהודה הנשיא, who argues with him, would say even that part is cancelled. That makes no sense. The whole point of taking collateral is to protect at least its own value. So the first reading must be wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (trying out a possible reading)
By implication, it follows that
Why?
Takes hold of, seizes

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהודה הנשיא never actually says that the part equal to the collateral is cancelled. The גמרא is showing that this would follow if we read the first opinion that way. That is why the reading is rejected.

phrases.english: If you say: the part equal to it,
phrases.notes: Meaning only the part of the debt that the collateral's value covers is not cancelled.

phrases.english: it follows that Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi holds:
even the part equal to it is cancelled?!
But then why does he take collateral?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵימָא כְּנֶגְדּוֹ מִכְּלָל דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה הַנָּשִׂיא סָבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries a first answer to the question in step 5 and shows it does not work.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל protects only the part of the debt equal to the collateral
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That reading would make רבי יהודה הנשיא hold that even the part equal to the collateral is cancelled. Then taking collateral would have no purpose.

steps.title: So they must be arguing about שמואל's rule
steps.stepSummary: Since the 'only the collateral's value' reading made no sense, the גמרא suggests that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל means the whole debt survives, so the תנאים argue about שמואל's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, doesn't he mean the whole debt survives? Then they are arguing about שמואל's rule.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof it started in step 4. Since the first reading ran into trouble, it suggests that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל means the entire debt is saved from שמיטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a משכון protects the entire debt, that matches שמואל's rule that collateral counts for the whole loan. רבי יהודה הנשיא would then disagree with שמואל. That would make שמואל's rule a real dispute between תנאים.

keyTerms.meaning: Equal to the whole of it (the entire debt)
Rather, is it not that (introduces the only remaining option)
They argue

phrases.english: Rather, is it not equal to the whole [debt]?
And they are arguing about שמואל's [rule]?
phrases.notes: שמואל's rule: a lender holding collateral is treated as owning it against the whole debt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Since step 6 seemed to rule out the 'only the collateral's value' reading, this step adopts the other reading to complete the proof.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's rule that collateral is considered equal to the whole debt
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא where רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says שמיטה does not cancel a loan backed by collateral, and רבי יהודה הנשיא disagrees

steps.title: No, they argue only about the collateral's share
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. Both sides agree the rest of the debt is cancelled. They argue only about the part equal to the collateral's value.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Really he means only the part equal to the collateral, and that is what they argue about. The first תנא says that part survives. רבי יהודה הנשיא says even that part is cancelled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back and returns to the first reading: only the amount the collateral is worth is saved. It then explains the dispute that way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With this reading, neither side is talking about שמואל's 'whole debt' rule, so the proof falls away. The argument is narrower. Does holding a משכון protect at least its own value from שמיטה, or not even that?

keyTerms.meaning: Really, in truth (we go back to the earlier reading)
Equal to it (only the collateral's value)
The first opinion in the ברייתא (here, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל)
Cancels the debt (through שמיטה)

phrases.english: No; really [he means only the part] equal to it,
and this is what they argue about:
the first תנא holds: [the part] equal to it [is not cancelled];
and רבי יהודה הנשיא holds:
[שמיטה] cancels [the part] equal to it too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 7's proof by going back to the reading that step 6 had challenged.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that the ברייתא shows שמואל's rule is a dispute between תנאים
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא can be read as arguing only about the collateral's own value, which has nothing to do with שמואל's 'whole debt' rule.

steps.title: Collateral can be just a reminder
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the question from step 6. According to רבי יהודה הנשיא, the lender takes the משכון simply as a reminder.
steps.simpleTranslation: And as for what you asked, 'Why take collateral at all?' It is just a reminder.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the question from step 6. If even the collateral's value is cancelled, why bother taking it? It answers: the collateral serves as a reminder of the loan.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 assumed collateral is only useful if it protects money. The answer shows it has another purpose: it keeps the debt in everyone's mind and pushes the borrower to pay. So רבי יהודה הנשיא's view makes sense after all.

keyTerms.meaning: And as for what you said (going back to answer an earlier question)
Collateral, a security item taken for a loan
As a reminder of the matter
Merely, just

steps.whatToRemember: In the end, the ברייתא does not prove that שמואל's rule is a dispute between תנאים. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and רבי יהודה הנשיא argue only about the collateral's own value. Even for רבי יהודה הנשיא, collateral still has a use as a reminder.

phrases.english: And as for what you said:
phrases.notes: This goes back to the question in step 6.

phrases.english: For what [purpose] does he take collateral from him?
Merely as a reminder of the matter.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּדְקָא אָמְרַתְּ: לְמַאי תָּפֵיס לֵיהּ מַשְׁכּוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the rejection in step 8 by answering the difficulty from step 6 that had forced the other reading.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 6's question about why a lender takes collateral according to רבי יהודה הנשיא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Offers a different purpose for the collateral
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Collateral is only useful if it protects money from שמיטה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Collateral can serve simply as a reminder of the debt.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing שבועת הדיינין
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula for the chapter שבועת הדיינין.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter שבועת הדיינין.
steps.whatsHappening: This line marks the end of the chapter שבועת הדיינין, the chapter about oaths that judges impose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No new argument here. It is the traditional farewell to a finished chapter, and it signals that a new chapter is about to start.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you (said at the end of a chapter)
The oath imposed by judges (name of the chapter)

phrases.english: We will return to you,
[chapter] 'The Oath of the Judges'

steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The chapter שבועת הדיינין is complete.

steps.title: Who swears and collects instead of swearing to be exempt
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה says a Torah oath normally frees the swearer from paying. It then lists five people who swear and collect money.
steps.simpleTranslation: Everyone who swears a Torah oath swears and does not pay. But these swear and collect: a hired worker, a robbed person, an injured person, someone whose opponent is suspected of lying under oath, and a storekeeper relying on his ledger.
steps.whatsHappening: A new chapter opens with a משנה. It sets a general rule about oaths and then lists exceptions where the oath lets a person take money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the defendant swears and walks away without paying. In these five cases the חכמים let the claimant swear and collect, even though he is not holding the money. The משנה will explain each case next.

keyTerms.meaning: They swear and do not pay (the oath frees them)
They swear and take (the oath lets them collect)
A hired worker
Suspected of swearing falsely
A storekeeper relying on his account book

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think everyone on this list swears a Torah oath. The rule is that Torah oaths free a person from paying. These five are special cases where the חכמים let the claimant swear and collect.
steps.whyThisMatters: This list sets the agenda for the whole new chapter. The גמרא will go through each of these cases one by one.

phrases.english: MISHNA: All who swear [an oath] of the Torah
swear and do not pay.
And these swear and take [payment]:
the hired worker, the one who was robbed, the one who was injured,
and one whose opponent is suspected regarding oaths,
and a storekeeper on his ledger.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Torah oaths free the swearer from paying. The שכיר, נגזל, נחבל, one whose opponent is suspected about oaths, and a חנווני with his ledger swear and collect.

steps.title: The hired worker swears and collects his wages
steps.stepSummary: A שכיר asks for his wages. The employer says he already paid, and the worker says he never got paid. The worker swears and collects. רבי יהודה says this only works if the employer admits part of the claim.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does it work for a hired worker? The worker says, 'Give me the wages you owe me.' The employer says, 'I already paid you.' The worker says, 'I never got them.' The worker swears and collects. רבי יהודה says the worker can only swear and collect if the employer admits part of the claim. For example, the worker says, 'Give me my fifty דינר of wages,' and the employer answers, 'You already got a gold דינר.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains the first of the five cases: a hired worker who swears that he was not paid and then collects his wages.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the defendant swears and is free. Here the worker, who is the one claiming money, swears and collects. רבי יהודה limits this. The worker swears only when the employer has already admitted part of the debt.

keyTerms.meaning: A hired worker
He swears and collects. The claimant takes the oath and gets paid.
A partial admission, where the defendant admits owing part of the claim
A gold דינר, a coin worth much more than a silver דינר

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up who is talking. The employer says 'I gave you the wages,' and the worker says 'I didn't take them.' The worker is the one who swears.

phrases.english: The hired worker – how does it work?
He said to him: Give me my wages
that you are holding for me;
he says: I already gave them,
and the other says: I did not take them
he swears and collects.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
Not unless there is a partial admission there.
How so? He said to him:
Give me my wages of fifty dinar
that you are holding for me,
and he says: You already received a gold dinar.
phrases.notes: A gold דינר is worth twenty-five silver ones, so the employer is admitting he still owes part of the money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first case from the list of five in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A hired worker who says he was not paid swears and collects. רבי יהודה requires that the employer admit part of the claim.

steps.title: The robbed person swears and collects
steps.stepSummary: Witnesses saw the defendant enter the claimant's house without permission to take collateral. The claimant says, 'You took my things,' and the defendant denies it. The claimant swears and collects. רבי יהודה requires a partial admission.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does it work for a person who was robbed? Witnesses testified that the defendant went into the claimant's house without permission to take collateral. The claimant says, 'You took my things.' The defendant says, 'I didn't take anything.' The claimant swears and collects. רבי יהודה says this only applies if there is a partial admission. For example, the claimant says, 'You took two things,' and the defendant says, 'I took only one.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains the second case: a person whose house was entered without permission. He swears about what was taken and collects.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The witnesses did not see anything being taken. They only saw the defendant go into the house without permission. That is enough for the claimant to swear and collect. רבי יהודה again says the defendant must admit part of the claim, here by admitting he took one item.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who was robbed
Testify, as witnesses do
To take collateral from him
Without permission or legal right

phrases.english: The robbed person – how does it work?
Witnesses were testifying about him
that he entered his house to take collateral without permission;
he says: You took my things,
and he says: I did not take them
he swears and collects.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: עַד שֶׁתְּהֵא שָׁם מִקְצָת הוֹדָאָה.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: Not unless there is a partial admission there.
How so? He said to him: You took two things,
and he says: I took only one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the hired worker to the second case in the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If witnesses saw someone enter a house without permission to take collateral, the owner swears about what was taken and collects. רבי יהודה requires a partial admission.

steps.title: The injured person swears and collects
steps.stepSummary: Witnesses saw the claimant go into the defendant's area unhurt and come out hurt. The claimant says, 'You hurt me,' and the defendant denies it. The claimant swears and collects. רבי יהודה requires a partial admission.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does it work for a person who was injured? Witnesses testified that he went into the defendant's control whole and came out injured. He says, 'You injured me,' and the defendant says, 'I didn't injure you.' The injured person swears and collects. רבי יהודה says this only applies if there is a partial admission. For example, he says, 'You injured me twice,' and the other says, 'I injured you only once.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains the third case: an injured person who swears that the defendant hurt him and then collects payment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The witnesses did not see the injury happen. They saw him go in healthy and come out hurt. That allows the injured person to swear and collect. רבי יהודה again needs the defendant to admit part of the claim, such as one injury out of two.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who was injured
Under his control, in the other person's area
Whole, unhurt
You injured me

phrases.english: The injured person – how does it work?
Witnesses were testifying about him

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנִּכְנַס תַּחַת יָדוֹ שָׁלֵם וְיָצָא חָבוּל;
phrases.english: that he went in under his control whole and came out injured;
and he said to him: You injured me,
and he says: I did not injure you
this one swears and collects.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: עַד שֶׁתְּהֵא שָׁם מִקְצָת הוֹדָאָה.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: Not unless there is a partial admission there.
How so? He said to him: You injured me twice,

phrases.aramaic: וְהַלָּה אוֹמֵר: ״לֹא חָבַלְתִּי בְּךָ אֶלָּא אֶחָת״.
phrases.english: and the other says: I injured you only once.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the robbed person to the third case in the list.
steps.whatToRemember: In all three cases so far (שכיר, נגזל, נחבל), the claimant swears and collects. Each time, רבי יהודה adds the same condition: the defendant must admit part of the claim.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If witnesses saw someone go in unhurt and come out hurt, he swears that the defendant injured him and collects. רבי יהודה requires a partial admission.

steps.title: Opening the case of a defendant who is not trusted to swear
steps.stepSummary: The משנה starts the fourth case: someone whose opponent is not trusted to take an oath.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does it work for someone whose opponent is suspected of swearing falsely?
steps.whatsHappening: This line only opens the fourth case. The משנה is setting up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the defendant would swear and be free. If the defendant cannot be trusted to swear, the משנה is about to explain how the claimant swears instead.

keyTerms.meaning: His opponent, the other side in the case
Suspected of swearing falsely, so not trusted to take an oath

phrases.english: One whose opponent is suspected regarding the oath – how does it work?
